_comment: How I work, as shown on the home page. Copy restates facts already in src/content/work; the broken-system example is read from the dental case study's first incident and rule at build time.

steps.p: Follow the number back to its source.
Fix the root, not the symptom, then prove it.
Write down what to check next time.

stages.p: Write down what the client means, not just what they said.
Turn it into numbered requirements. Mark what is still open.
Keep the architecture stable while decisions are still pending.
A working demo the client can react to, traced to the requirements.
Production, documentation, and a codebase someone else can own.

cases.ask: A SaaS that turns public filings into sales-ready leads. Requirements arrived in rounds.
cases.got: Requirements, architecture and detailed design, plus a deployed demo for client review.
cases.how: Three decisions stayed open, so I designed around them. Every requirement ID traces to a screen.

cases.ask: Automate expense claims inside the ERP. Then the goal moved to procurement for two companies.
cases.got: AI agents working inside a live ERP: two live deployments, demo and production.
cases.how: I reused the same agent layer for the new goal instead of starting over.

cases.ask: Turn chatter from Telegram, Discord and X into something searchable, with alerts.
cases.got: A backend built alone: ingestion, AI summaries, semantic search and alerts. 154 of 155 commits.
cases.how: Built so the client's own team could take it over, then handed over at their request.

path.p: Android and web games in Unity and PlayCanvas.
